core.headline: End-of-terrace Victorian cottage in Smarden Conservation Area
core.summary: Guide Price £425,000. An end-of-terrace Victorian cottage in the Smarden Conservation Area, built c.1880 of red brick under a clay-tiled roof, with a cast-iron fireplace, quarry-tiled kitchen floor and cottage garden.
core.listing:
An end-of-terrace Victorian cottage in the Smarden Conservation Area, built c.1880 of red brick under a clay-tiled roof. The property offers two bedrooms, a cast-iron fireplace in the sitting room and a quarry-tiled kitchen floor.

The sitting room measures 3.90m x 3.60m (12'10" x 11'10") and has a cast-iron fireplace. The kitchen/dining room measures 4.30m x 3.20m (14'1" x 10'6") and has a quarry-tiled floor, reclaimed beams and a range alcove. Ledged-and-braced doors are fitted throughout.

On the first floor, bedroom one measures 3.80m x 3.30m (12'6" x 10'10") and bedroom two measures 2.90m x 2.40m (9'6" x 7'10"). There is one bathroom.

To the rear is a cottage garden of approx. 12m (40ft) with a brick path and a timber shed.

The village pub is approx. 2 minutes' walk. Parking is on-street.

Guide Price £425,000. Freehold. Council Tax Band C (Ashford Borough Council). EPC rating E. Construction: standard – red brick under a clay-tiled roof. Electricity: mains. Water: mains (not metered). Sewerage: septic tank. Heating: oil-fired central heating. Broadband: FTTC. Mobile signal: good outdoors, variable indoors. The property is within the Smarden Conservation Area. The septic tank is shared with 1 Forge Cottages and located in its garden; access rights for maintenance; emptying costs shared. The rear of the garden is in Flood Zone 2 (Environment Agency map); the house has not flooded. The seller does not know whether the shared septic tank meets the Environment Agency's 2020 general binding rules. There is restricted head height at the top of the stairs, approx. 1.88m (6'2").
